problemsData.heading:
Common Setup Problems 
 & How We Design Them Out
problemsData.subhead: Most faults in experience center AV solutions trace back to early planning. We resolve each one during survey and design.

problem.title: Daylight washes out the screens
problem.text: Glass facades and spotlights flatten the image, so key visuals look faded by midday.

solution.title: Brightness set from light readings
solution.text: We measure ambient light at the survey and pick displays with enough brightness.

problem.title: Echo makes the host hard to follow
problem.text: Hard floors and glass walls reflect sound around the room and blur each spoken word.

solution.title: Audio tuned to the wall finishes
solution.text: Speaker layouts and DSP equalization are matched to the wall materials in each zone.
solution.tag: Speech stays clear at each stop

problem.title: Captions unreadable from the back
problem.text: Screens sized for the front of the group leave guests at the rear squinting at text.

solution.title: Image height set by the farthest guest
solution.text: Display dimensions are calculated from the farthest viewing point in your room.

problem.title: Touch screens lag or freeze
problem.text: Interactive demos stall mid-session and guests give up after the second or third tap.

solution.title: Hardware sized for the software
solution.text: Players and PCs match the real content load and are tested with the final build.

problem.title: Equipment overheats in joinery
problem.text: Racks and LED panels sealed inside cabinets build heat and shut down during visits.

solution.title: Heat & power planned with MEP
solution.text: Load and cooling figures go to your MEP contractor before any joinery is detailed.

problem.title: Screens do not match each other
problem.text: Neighboring displays show different colors and brightness, which breaks the story.

solution.title: Displays calibrated at commissioning
solution.text: Color and brightness are matched across panels and projection edges are blended.

faqHeaderData.heading:
Common Questions on 
 Experience Center & Demo Rooms

faqData.question: How long does an experience center project take in Dubai?
faqData.answer: Project timelines for experience center solutions in Dubai typically range from ten to sixteen weeks from site survey to final handover. Survey and design work occupy the first month. Equipment lead times, especially for custom displays, drive the core schedule. On-site installation aligns with your fit-out timeline once the site is cleared.

faqData.question: Can you build a demo room inside an occupied office tower?
faqData.answer: Yes, our team can build demo room solutions inside active corporate towers. Noisy work is scheduled during approved evening or weekend hours, and materials move through designated service elevators. These operational windows are integrated into the main schedule during planning to protect business continuity.

faqData.question: Will you work alongside our architect and fit-out contractor?
faqData.answer: Yes, technical coordination with your appointed architect and interior contractor is standard practice. Engineering teams participate in site coordination meetings and merge AV schematics directly into master architectural drawings. Early coordination locks in cabling routes, wall backing, and power locations before wall construction closes.

faqData.question: Do you handle equipment import and customs clearance?
faqData.answer: Procurement, shipping, and customs clearance are managed entirely as part of our experience center AV integration services. Equipment featuring wireless transmission technology undergoes local regulatory type approval prior to customs release. This administrative step is scheduled early during procurement to prevent project delays.

faqData.question: What is a workable room size for a product demo space?
faqData.answer: A functional product demo space requires a minimum floor area of 25 square meters. Smaller footprints restrict display size and force visitors too close to screen surfaces. Layouts requiring immersive rooms with multiple demonstration zones generally start at 100 square meters to allow comfortable guest movement.

faqData.question: Can an existing showroom be converted into a demo room?
faqData.answer: Yes, converting an existing space into a functional demo room is a common and efficient option. Site surveys evaluate existing power circuits, ceiling capacity, and cable pathways to identify reusable infrastructure. Primary technical factors include slab-to-slab height for large displays and total electrical load capacity.

faqData.question: How do you decide between LED and projection for a wall?
faqData.answer: Display selection depends on ambient lighting, viewing distances, and wall geometry. Direct-view LED maintains contrast in bright spaces and supports close-up viewing with fine pixel pitches. Projection covers large, curved surfaces cost-effectively. Deploying smart demo room automation allows both display types to operate in an executive briefing center design.

faqData.question: Can the room bring in remote visitors during a live session?
faqData.answer: Yes, interactive demo room technology enables remote participants to join live sessions seamlessly. Integrated camera positions and multi-zone microphones allow virtual attendees to follow the presenter throughout the space. Remote meeting controls are embedded directly into the primary touch panel used by the presenter.

faqData.question: Do you produce the content that plays on the screens?
faqData.answer: Yes, content creation is available alongside our corporate experience center setup services. When we deliver the media, visuals are rendered to match the display dimensions precisely. If your marketing team or agency manages creative work, our team provides target resolutions, aspect ratios, and file formats ahead of time.

faqData.question: Who operates and maintains an executive briefing center after handover?
faqData.answer: Your internal team manages daily operations using training provided during commissioning. Continuous system monitoring, preventive maintenance, and guaranteed repair response times are included under a signed service agreement. Pay-per-call technical support remains available without an ongoing contract across all executive briefing center solutions.
